title.narrative: Enhancing resilience and mitigating the impact of winter conditions through an integrated response (Education, NFI, and Early Recovery and Livelihoods) in Aleppo and Ar-Raqqa (Sub-objectives 1 and 2)

description.narrative: ltpgtThe proposal's strategy is to provide immediate relief during winter while simultaneously creating long-term perspectives for the affected population. The project aims to ensure survival through winter and facilitate children's access to education, tackling barriers related to family income, and enhancing community resilience through income-generating initiatives linked to community improvement plans. This dual approach is designed to break the cycle of vulnerability, creating a foundation for sustained well-being beyond the immediate challenges of the winter of 2023/2024.ltbrgtIn Aleppo governorate, Abu Jabar and Ar-raqqa, Debsi Faraj area, economic challenges, inadequate education, and poverty contribute to children being out of school or at risk of dropping out. FCA’s needs assessment of September 2023, shows high levels of need and vulnerability. The earthquake and displacement worsened the situation, and winter poses additional challenges for families. Post-crisis economic struggles persist and cause a lack of sustainable income at the household level, resulting in families resorting to negative coping mechanisms: dropping out of school, child labor, and early marriage. The project addresses education and winter-related needs, re-enrolling out-of-school children (OOSC) through a BTL campaign and remedial classes. The project builds teacher capacity and incentivizes transportation. To tackle economic challenges, some parents/caregivers receive financial support for business growth. Community-led initiatives enhance recovery and build resilience. Winterization efforts provide essential items and access of vulnerable families for survival in the harsh winter season. In September 2024, military escalations in Lebanon, had forced many families to flee to Syria carrying nothing except of their minimum documentation. This was followed with a military operation covering whole Syria in November, resulted in control shift except for Ar-Raqqah and north-east Syria, a place for military and political negotiations under Kurdish control with no accessibility for FCA and no ability to complete its activities in the originally targeted locations. A return influx was witnessed internally or from the neighbouring countries towards Aleppo, especially the most vulnerable whom didn’t have valid documentation in the hosting countries. FCA conducted a rapid needs assessment in coordination with humanitarian actors and sector coordinators, in addition to authorities’ representatives in Aleppo, revealing the huge needs of returnees.ltbrgtProposed activities: lt/pgtltpgtWinterization NFIs: lt/pgtltpgt- Distribute core items to 280 households (1680 individuals)lt/pgtltpgt- Provide cash for winter assistance to 259 returnee Households in Urban settings (1295 individuals).ltbrgtEducation:lt/pgtltpgt Rehabilitate classrooms (23) and WASH facilities at 1 schoolltbrgt Provide solar power systems at 1 schoolltbrgt Deliver non-formal education programs, catch-up classes, and literacy programs to 1080 childrenltbrgt Conduct Back-to-Learning (BTL) campaign reaching 100 children and their parentsltbrgt Supply school materials to 1450 children, especially those with disabilities.ltbrgt Support 2024 exams for 500 9th and12th graders.ltbrgt Provide professional development to 15 teaching staff.ltbrgt Establish 1 Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs).ltbrgt Provide school furniture to 1 schools.ltbrgt Work with SARC to provide transportation (10 buses across 14 days) for crossline students to attend national examsltbrgt Provide 2000 mattresses for children inside the crossline accommodation centres in Aleppo Cityltbrgt Provide transportation for SARC to issue 1500 mattresses, 12500 blankets and 2400 mobile lights to the accommodation centres in Aleppo and RaqqaltbrgtEarly Recovery and Livelihoods:ltbrgt Support 32 small business owners financially.ltbrgt Assist in creating and implementing community early recovery plans.ltbrgtFCA is proposing a 2 months No-cost Extension, to cover the most-in-need sufficiently.ltbrgtlt/pgt
